tokens.SUBJECT: Science
tokens.CONTENT_STANDARD: B7.2.1 Demonstrate understanding of mixtures and separation.
tokens.LEARNING_INDICATOR:
B7.2.1.1 Describe mixtures
B7.2.1.2 Separate mixtures
tokens.PERFORMANCE_INDICATOR:
Explain filtration using a diagram
Separate a sand-and-water mixture
tokens.PHASE_1_STARTER:
- Show muddy water and ask how it can be made clear.
- Predict what happens to muddy water in a funnel.
tokens.PHASE_2_MAIN:
- Learners filter their own sample in pairs.
- Demonstrate folding filter paper and pouring the mixture.
- Class Assignment: Draw and label the filtration setup.
tokens.PHASE_3_PLENARY:
- Summarise that filtration separates insoluble solids.
- Home Assignment: List three household examples of filtration.
tokens.EVALUATION: Observe each pair's filtration and question their choices.

appendix.text: Assessment Structure — Week 1 (Lesson 1)
Assignments
Class assignment: Draw and label the filtration setup.
Home assignment: List three household examples of filtration.
Assessment Questions / Checks (with marking)
• Why does the filter paper trap sand? (DoK 2)
Expected evidence: Names particle size as the reason.
Marking: Accept any answer naming particle size.
Watch for: Sand dissolves in water.
If not reached: Re-demonstrate with a transparent mixture.
Marking Rubric for the Learner Task
Filter a sand-and-water mixture safely.
Criterion: Correct setup
4 — exceeds the standard: Funnel and paper seated correctly. (4 pt)
3 — meets the standard: Minor spillage only. (3 pt)
Total marks: 4
Award for a working setup.
School assessment policy.
